- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Forecast mean is consistently higher than true mean, suggesting a persistent upward bias.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, possibly due to reduced volatility or lagging adjustment.
- Model reacts too slowly to recent price drops — fails to anticipate downward corrections.
- In periods of high volatility, model overfits recent trends and fails to account for mean reversion.
- Forecasting horizon >15 days shows increasing divergence from true values, suggesting model struggles with long-term trend capture.
- Model often fails to adjust for seasonal or calendar-driven patterns (e.g., end-of-month or holiday effects).
